thread:
maria: uploaded an nsys capture from tonight's nightly perf run — seeing a weird HBM waveform with repeated drops and a mid-trace kernel fallback to a simpler attention kernel around 820ms. link: https://perfetto.local/trace/1753000011 :thinking_face:

samir: which model/run? is this the long-seqlen sampling job?

maria: yes — redwood-v1-small quantized. we sampled mixed seqlens (256 -> 4096) in the same capture to exercise batching heuristics. observed pattern: first ~300ms low BW (warmup), then a big spike, then periodic drops and a kernel switch at ~0.82s.

alex: can you paste the kernel timeline slice + nsys stats? curious if kernels themselves are stalling or if DMA/PCI interplay kills BW.

maria: timeline snippet:
```
0.00s - 0.80s  attention_fused (kernels mostly small matmuls, sustained HBM ~110GB/s)
0.82s          attention_simple (fallback) — HBM BW drops to ~28GB/s for ~40ms
0.87s - 1.10s fused resumes but with oscillating BW
```
nsys summary: DRAM throughput: avg 95GB/s, peaks 125GB/s, troughs 20-30GB/s; observed sudden rise in KV cache miss ratio when seqlen crossed page boundary.

jess: that fits a KV warmup/miss-storm theory. if the kernel selection happens based on instantaneous latency/throughput without accounting for KV heating, we can flip to a kernel that expects hot KV and starve HBM while misses resolve.

samir: i suspect microbatch boundary alignment triggered at padding->1024 tokens and forced a new kernel choice mid-request. the mismatch between predicted token distribution and actual led to inconsistent kernel choices.

perfbot: [auto] Trace analysis flagged: hbw-oscillation, mid-kernel-switch, kv-miss-storm. See /traces/alerts/1753000011.json

alex: two quick experiments to try: (1) short hold-window before applying a new kernel selection (e.g. hold 50-80ms) to let KV warms settle; (2) gate kernel escalation on KV hit-rate (requires lightweight counter). also try `--kv-warmup-only` mode to force prefetch.

maria: i applied a quick patch with hold=60ms on the routing heuristic and re-ran a subset. results: kernel flip frequency dropped 70% but p99 tail latency increased ~3%. attached nvprof memcopy timeline snippet for the run:
```
==PROF== MemCopy time breakdown
HtoD: 4.2ms
DtoH: 3.8ms
GDR copy bursts align with the BW spikes around 0.4s and 0.9s
```

jess: thanks — the tradeoff is expected. instead of a fixed hold window we should incorporate a short running average of KV hit rate and only escalate if hit_rate > 0.85. that avoids unnecessary tail increase for steady workloads but still protects for cold starts.

samir: +1. we can expose a perf counter: l2_hit_ratio and dram_bw_sample in the kernel decision path. cheaper than waiting arbitrary ms.

alex: if you want to experiment quickly: patch lines in runtime heuristics:
```
# pseudocode
if kv_hit_rate_last_10_batches > 0.85 and predicted_latency_gain > threshold:
    select_fused_kernel()
else if time_since_last_switch < hold_ms:
    keep_current_kernel()
```

maria: i'll run A/B tonight across three arms: baseline, hold-window(60ms), and hit-rate-gating(0.85). running on g5.12 cluster — kicking off now and will upload traces. :coffee:

alex: please include perf counters for l2 hit ratio and dram_bw sample in the upload so we can correlate. if the hit-rate-gating shows no tail regression, that's our winner.

maria: traces will be in /mnt/traces/eng-runtime/1753000011/ (nsys + perfetto + nvprof). cc @eng-runtime. will post results tomorrow morning.
